_doc: WHERE EACH CHANNEL'S SEQUENTIAL REPEATERS LIVE (docs/physical.md, 'Wrappers and links').

Every block instance sits in a hardening wrapper of the same name (fet, lane_05, ...), and every channel instance runs from its source's wrapper to its destination's. A LINK entry says how many repeater stages (rtl/phys/ccv_common_rpt.sv) each wrapper along that path holds. Any channel instance no entry covers is 'src:0 > dst:0': abutted, no repeaters.
channel  the channel name without ccv_, e.g. fet_dec_instr

copies   which copies of a replicated channel (rcu_lane_ops has 32): "all" (the default), or a list such as [5, 6]. An entry naming copies beats an "all" entry for those copies; any other overlap is an error.

route    the hops, in the direction of valid, as 'wrapper:stages' separated by '>'. It starts at 'src' and ends at 'dst', this copy's own endpoints. Anything between is a FEEDTHROUGH: another wrapper the channel crosses, named by its block instance ('miu', 'lane_06'), which gets ports for it and holds its stages.
why      optional: a note for the reader.
Rules, checked by tools/ccv_links.py whenever the generators run:
- stages are whole numbers, 0 to 16; the end at EXTERNAL holds none (it has no wrapper);
- a route doesn't pass its own endpoints, or any wrapper twice;
- every copy of a lockstep channel has the same total, or lockstep delivery is lost, and the same src stages, since the checker bank watches each link where it leaves the source's wrapper.
- a channel declaring latency_match in the schema (ccv_ooe_fet_ckpt_free, with ccv_ooe_fet_redirect: A-58) has the same total as its partner, so the two arrive in the order they were sent.

What a link's total N changes, derived from this file and nowhere else: its checkers' ROUND_TRIP (+2N, and so their DEPTH, the credit loop), TIMEOUT_N (+2N) and SRC_STAGES, and the C++ skeleton's latency and credit depth for that slot (CCV_CREDIT_DEPTH + 2N, full bandwidth: Q-43), so both hosts still agree.

hard_reuse: block types whose wrappers must stay hard-reusable. Their instances are grouped by what their wrapper holds -- each end's stages, each feedthrough's channel and stages -- and each group is one TEMPLATE with its stages fixed and no parameters: ccv_<type>_w for the group most instances are in, ccv_<type>_w_v1, _v2, ... for the rest, so a divergent split costs exactly as many templates as it has distinct wrappers, and no more. A type not listed gets one parameterised module (stages set by the top) and a module of its own per instance with feedthroughs.

no_flop: the channel ends built WITHOUT a boundary flop. Every other end's repeater holds one (rtl/phys/ccv_common_rpt.sv, BOUNDARY 1; Daniel, 2026-11-05): the block's own boundary register, built in its wrapper, the sender's last flop or the receiver's first, which CCV_RT_ABUT already counts (AR's rev 285). An entry names a block type (or a list) and "channels": "all" (the default) or a list of channel names without ccv_, with a why. Allowed only where the block's own register drives or takes the port with 0 NGD, which tools/check-ngd.py holds at the block's wrapper, or for a DPI host, whose posedge block is that register (AR's rev 287 (1)). "all" is refused for a block whose top is RTL: an RTL block replacing a stub takes the flops in that same change, never inheriting the stub's no-flop. "except" (with "all" only) leaves the named channels flopped. A flopped RECEIVING end adds one cycle to its crossing, bnd_rx (AR's revs 300 and 301): a crossing is CCV_LAT_HOP + link_n + bnd_rx, in params/ccv_params.json's derives (bnd_rx('channel')) and in both hosts' links; a flopped sending end adds none, since it replaces the sender's own output register (AR's rev 285).

no_flop.why: DPI hosts: every block's top is the C++ skeleton over DPI-C (rtl/top/dpi/) or a generated stub, whose posedge block is the boundary register at 0 NGD; dropping it would move both hosts' sampling and gain no contract (AR's rev 287 (1)). Each block leaves this list when its RTL top replaces the stub. RCU is the next entry.

Option 1 (AR's rev 301): RCU puts logic before its first register on these three inputs, so each takes the boundary flop in its wrapper and its crossing counts bnd_rx = 1 (AR's rev 300). Every other RCU end is taken or driven by a register at 0 NGD, as a DPI host's posedge block is (AR's rev 287 (1)).
